claims.text: High-energy forging followed by sub-transus annealing will produce a bimodal grain structure in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed bimodal microstructure will increase tensile ductility.
The proposed bimodal microstructure will increase uniform tensile elongation.
The proposed processing route will preserve the alloy's high strength.
The proposed processing route will preserve impact-triggered energy release.
Conventionally processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a relatively uniform refractory multiphase microstructure.
High-energy forging will refine the microstructure of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Sub-transus annealing after forging will create both ultrafine and coarser equiaxed grains.
Fine grains will retain high strength through grain-boundary hardening.
Coarser grains will facilitate plastic deformation and delay strain localization.
Larger grains will accommodate strain through more extensive dislocation motion and crack blunting.
The processed alloy will exhibit a 30–50% increase in uniform tensile elongation relative to the stated baseline.
The processed alloy will retain a yield strength above approximately 750 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported yield strength of 786 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
HfZrTiTa0.53 has a reported terminal strain of 13.5% in tension.
The proposed property improvements apply at room and moderately elevated temperatures under quasi-static and high-strain-rate loading.
Behavior may differ at temperatures or strain rates outside the reported range.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% value is alternately treated as terminal strain, tensile elongation to failure, and uniform tensile elongation. These are distinct measurements, so the baseline used for the claimed 30% improvement is internally inconsistent.
